name: Morning height measurement trick

lead: People are slightly taller in the morning than in the evening, so measuring just after getting out of bed gives your highest figure of the day. Forum users use it to report a higher number and to track height-related changes on a consistent basis.

Spinal discs compress during upright activity and recover when lying down, so stature falls over the day and returns overnight. One study cited by Wikipedia found children's heights dropped by a mean of about 1.5 cm between waking and mid-afternoon, and clinical practice uses a stadiometer with standardised posture as the reference method.

paras: People measure shortly after waking, barefoot against a wall or stadiometer, at the same time each day so readings can be compared. Posture, shoes and measurement technique add further variation, and some forum posters also discuss supplements, core strength and insoles for keeping morning height through the day, though no studies were found supporting those.

There are no meaningful health risks in measuring. The main caveat is measurement error: a typical error of about half a centimetre can hide small real changes, and self-reported heights tend to differ from measured values.

chain: Spine is least compressed after waking
angle.text: Measuring shortly after waking, when the spine is least compressed, records your daily maximum height, a figure about a centimetre or more above the evening reading. It also gives a consistent baseline for tracking height changes.

lead: The morning height measurement trick is the practice of measuring height shortly after waking, when it is at its daily maximum, instead of later in the day. It is discussed on height and looksmaxxing forums as a way to report a higher figure, to track results of height-related interventions consistently, or to decide what a person's 'real' height is.

Wikipedia reports that height changes over the day, that lying down for long periods tends to increase it and vigorous exercise before measuring tends to reduce it, and cites a study of 100 children whose heights fell by a mean of 1.54 cm between getting out of bed and mid-afternoon [1]. Clinical practice uses a stadiometer, a vertical ruler with a sliding headpiece, with the subject barefoot and standing erect against it [2].
Forum posters also discuss ways to keep morning height through the day, including supplements, core strength and insoles, claims for which no supporting studies were found.
infobox: About 1.5 cm lower by late afternoon [1]
Night height, true height, self-reported height

paras: Standing height is measured with a stadiometer in children over two and adults who can stand unaided; shorter or less mobile subjects are measured lying down or estimated with surrogates such as knee height, arm span or ulna length [1][3]. Wikipedia notes that measurement error is a limitation, and that a typical error of 0.5 cm can make small real growth look like negative growth or more than it is [1].

Grokipedia describes the reference measurement protocol as barefoot with heels, buttocks, shoulders and head against the backboard, and states that tape measures can add variability from sagging or inconsistent application [2]. A study of vertebral fractures reports that serial height measurement is used to monitor height loss in older adults [4].

A National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey analysis examined how age affects the validity of self-reported height, weight and body mass index [5]. Self-reported height is a different matter from the morning-versus-night question, but it is relevant because online discussions of the practice often involve what height a person states.

A thread titled around night versus morning height has a user reporting about 179.7 cm at night and about 181 cm in the morning and asking whether the average is his real height; replies agree the midpoint would be about 180.35 cm. Another thread lists glucosamine, a stronger core and lower back, and heel insoles as things the poster says help maintain morning height through the day.

No studies found on the morning height measurement trick itself or on glucosamine, core training or insoles for retaining morning height. Related research includes the child study of diurnal height change cited by Wikipedia [1], measurement work on height loss in older adults [4], and studies of self-reported height [5].

lore.intro: On looksmaxxing forums, morning versus night height is a recurring question about which figure counts as a person's height.

claims.claim: Morning height is higher than evening height.
